newsitem.title: FRANCE: Latest EU grain forecast 199.8 million tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Latest EU grain forecast 199.8 million tonnes.

text.p: Latest European Commission grain forecasts given to farm ministries point to a total 1997 harvest of 199.778 million tonnes compared with a record 205.466 million tonnes last year, EU member country sources said on Friday.

The figures, distributed on Thursday, also suggest a fall in the durum harvest to around 7.5 million tonnes from last year's crop near nine million after drought in Mediterranean producing states, they said.
The figures have not been officially published, although a senior Commission official has been quoted as telling an industry group that the crop would be around 200 million.
Details of other internal Commission estimates for soft wheat, barley and other grains were not immediately available.

Grain trade organisation Coceral, which projects a slightly lower crop of 197.289 million tonnes, said on July 4 that overall output should include 88.43 million for soft wheat, 50.85 million for barley and 33.37 million for maize.

The Commission's figures are being kept under review as more of this year's heavy crop is brought in, as well as to take account of changes suggested by member states at expert-level talks in Brussels on Thursday.
Grain sources said none of these were major but that had not prevented alarm bells ringing on Friday over what had seemed to be a drastic cut in Italy's maize area, amid wide confusion.

Italy was thought by several states to have revised its maize area to 630,000 hectares from the Commission's figure of 1.050 million. But one source said the figure that emerged later was a more plausible 1.035 million and there may have been errors in translation. Confirmation was not yet available.
